patch.value: Context usage-feedback and next/context author resolution bypass the harness identity contract: every mutation without PM_AUTHOR silently fails to record affinity

Three call sites resolve the acting author as process.env.PM_AUTHOR ?? settings.author_default instead of calling the canonical resolveAuthorIdentity precedence chain, so the harness-detected identity shipped by pm-z9x1r2 is invisible to them: src/cli/main.ts:734 (afterCommand context-usage hook), src/cli/commands/context.ts:2597, and src/cli/commands/next.ts:308 and :662. In this repository author_default is the empty string, so an agent that relies on automatic identity detection - the documented default and the workflow the product deliberately optimizes for - resolves to an empty author. recordContextUsageTouches then throws TypeError('Context usage touch requires author and intent'), the throw is swallowed, and every mutation prints 'afterCommand hook_warnings=context_usage_feedback_write_failed'. Reproduced on ten consecutive pm update invocations on 2026-07-25; the same runs recorded author 'harness:claude-code' with author_source 'detected' in history, proving the detection layer works and only these read/hook paths ignore it.

The context-usage hook, pm next, and pm context resolve the acting identity through the single canonical resolver (resolveAuthorIdentity / resolveAuthor) rather than reading PM_AUTHOR and author_default directly; A workspace with an empty author_default and no PM_AUTHOR records usage touches under the detected harness identity and emits no hook warning; recordContextUsageTouches surfaces a typed, named error instead of a bare TypeError so the swallowed-throw path can never hide a systemic outage again; A contract test asserts that no source file outside core/shared/author.ts reads process.env.PM_AUTHOR, making the bypass class mechanically impossible to reintroduce; Usage affinity accumulated under a detected identity is stable across invocations of the same harness
Author identity is resolved once, by one contract, on every path that needs it
Usage affinity is an input to context relevance ranking; losing it for the default agent workflow silently degrades the quality of every pm context and pm next answer without any visible failure.
Restores the usage-feedback signal for harness-identified agents, removes a warning printed on every mutation that trains operators to ignore warnings, and closes the bypass class with a gate.
One author-resolution contract, no direct PM_AUTHOR reads outside it, no hook warning on the default path, and usage affinity recorded for detected identities.
Harness detection shipped and closed on 2026-07-25; the paths that were supposed to consume it were never migrated, so the feature is half-live and its main downstream consumer is dark.

patch.value: Stops new unknown-author history events from being generated on every create, which would otherwise re-open the governance warning that was just closed; restores the usage-affinity signal for harness-identified agents; and closes the whole duplicated-precedence class with one contract test.

create and copy resolve the acting identity through the canonical resolver instead of a private selectAuthor, so an item created with no PM_AUTHOR and an empty author_default carries the detected harness identity and not the literal 'unknown'; The context-usage hook, pm next, and pm context resolve identity through the same canonical resolver; A workspace with an empty author_default and no PM_AUTHOR records usage touches under the detected identity and emits no hook warning; recordContextUsageTouches raises a typed, named error instead of a bare TypeError, so a swallowed throw can never hide a systemic outage again; A contract test asserts that process.env.PM_AUTHOR is read in exactly one source file and that no other module defines a private author-precedence helper, making the bypass class mechanically impossible to reintroduce; Items created during this session that were stamped 'unknown' are dispositioned through the existing acknowledgment flow rather than by rewriting history

The canonical precedence chain lives in core/shared/author.ts (resolveAuthorIdentity: explicit argument, then PM_AUTHOR, then configured default, then detected harness, then unknown). Six presentation-layer sites re-implement it and all of them omit the harness-detection step, so the identity capability that shipped and closed on 2026-07-25 is invisible to them. Two distinct failures result. (1) Attribution: src/cli/commands/create.ts:1352 and src/cli/commands/copy.ts:74 each define a private selectAuthor that resolves explicit ?? PM_AUTHOR ?? settings.author_default and falls back to the literal 'unknown'. With author_default empty - the state of this repository - every item created by a harness-identified agent is stamped author: unknown and writes an unknown-author history event, which is precisely the governance warning that pm-zqpnte just finished dispositioning. Verified on pm-42p9nk, pm-wt43zj, and pm-tuadp2: item author 'unknown' and the create history entry author 'unknown' with author_source 'unknown', while the very next pm update on the same items recorded 'harness:claude-code' with author_source 'detected'. (2) Relevance: src/cli/main.ts:734 (afterCommand context-usage hook), src/cli/commands/context.ts:2597, and src/cli/commands/next.ts:308 and :662 read PM_AUTHOR ?? author_default directly; the empty result makes recordContextUsageTouches throw TypeError('Context usage touch requires author and intent'), the throw is swallowed, and every mutation prints 'afterCommand hook_warnings=context_usage_feedback_write_failed'. Reproduced on every mutation in this session.
Author-resolution bypass class: create/copy and the context, next, and usage-feedback paths re-implement author precedence without harness detection, stamping author 'unknown' on new items
